All tropical cyclone-related watches and warnings were cancelled 
today for the Marianas as Super Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to 
move away from the region. However, winds will remain moderate to 
strong over Saipan and Tinian, increasing to near-gale over Rota and 
Guam. A ridge will build in following Champi's exit beginning Monday
night, lasting through at least Tuesday, allowing a drier regime to
develop. In the late week, scattered showers may return ahead of 
broad troughs entering the region from the east.

Marine...
A Typhoon Warning has been cancelled for Guam and Rota waters. 
Combined seas of 13 to 16 feet for Guam waters, 11 to 15 feet for
Rota waters, and 10 to 14 feet for Tinian and Saipan waters are 
expected tonight. As Champi continues moving away at a relatively 
quick speed, seas could drop below 15 feet after midnight for Guam
and Rota waters. Due to sea conditions remaining hazardous to 
small craft, a Small Craft Advisory remains in effect for Tinian 
and Saipan waters until at least Monday afternoon. Hazardous surf 
and high rip current risk is expected along south and west facing 
reefs of the Marianas, as Super Typhoon Champi continues to move away
from the area while its emanating swells continue to pummel the 
shores at least through Monday afternoon. A moderate risk of rip 
currents is expected along north and east facing reefs through 
Monday, to then drop to low along north reefs thereafter. A moderate 
risk of lightning is expected through at least Monday night.

Hydrology...
As Super Typhoon Champi (29W) continues to move west, away from the 
Marianas, convectively active outer rain bands associated with Champi
will produce locally heavy rainfall tonight. Conditions are expected
to improve around midnight, so the Flood Watch may be cancelled if
conditions warrant.

Tropical Systems...
Super Typhoon (STY) Champi (29W) is currently located near 13.1N 
142.1E, or roughly 170 miles west of Guam, as it continues moving 
westward and away from the coastal waters. Champi's eye, and 
the destructive conditions within its compact eyewall, narrowly 
missed Guam early this morning,For more information, please refer to the bulletins issued by the 
Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW, and by 
the National Weather Service in Tiyan, Guam under WMO header WTPQ32 
PGUM. passing just 10 miles south of Guam's southern tip at around 
4:26 AM ChST. This was just before it was upgraded to a dangerous 
Category 4 Super Typhoon with maximum sustained winds of 150 mph 
within the eyewall. STY Champi remains at this intensity as it moves 
westward away from the area this evening, then is expected to weaken 
slightly on Monday, before strengthening once more through Monday 
night. Champi may intensify to Category 5 around Tuesday afternoon as
it continues northwestward over the Philippine Sea, well north of 
Yap. As of the latest STY Champi Public Advisory (#15a), the Typhoon 
Warning is cancelled for Guam and Rota, and no tropical cyclone 
watches or warnings remain in effect across the Marianas or coastal 
waters.

For more information, please refer to the bulletins issued by the 
Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW, and by 
the National Weather Service in Tiyan, Guam under WMO header WTPQ32 
PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Not a lot going on in eastern Micronesia this afternoon. Partly
cloudy skies across the region with isolated showers. For Majuro, as
STY Champi continues west across the Philippine Sea, it will drag the
monsoon trough over the Marshalls, resulting in Majuro seeing a brief
period of scattered showers later this evening. For Pohnpei and 
Kosrae, the dry pattern looks to continue until midweek. At this 
time, the monsoon trough is expected to be pulled over the area by 
Champi, bringing a round of showers to Kosrae and Pohnpei, with POPs 
(Probability of Precipitation) at 30 to 50 percent Wednesday into 
Thursday for Pohnpei and 30 to 40 percent for Kosrae Wednesday. After
these showers move through, expect a dry pattern to return to the 
islands. Majuro can expect to see a couple more brief rounds of
showers Monday night and Tuesday night, with POPs between 30 and 40
percent. From Wednesday on, a dry pattern will dominate.

Benign marine conditions will continue through the week, with seas
between 3 and 5 feet and mostly light to gentle winds.

Western Micronesia...
The main weather producer over western Micronesia will be Super
Typhoon Champi and the monsoon trough. As Champi moves west across
the Philippine Sea, it is expected to enhance a monsoon surge across
palau and Yap. This surge will feed into Champi, bringing a feeder
bands with scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to Yap 
Monday and to Palau Tuesday. Convection decrease over Palau Tuesday
